walkthrough: Goal: colour under light (光色, unit 7): predicting what a light's colour and its surroundings do to a local colour: the light side takes the light's colour, the shadow the sky's and goes darker, and the object's own colour stays in both. Each region's colour is read directly, but the rules are a model's, so the marks are help and my eye judges (D123).

Entry: unit 7's tile Colour under light (after placement), or Start when it is next; no pack is needed. A lesson holds one scene, about 6 minutes: level 1 a box, a cylinder and a sphere in turn, white or light grey on a grey ground, a warm sun and a blue sky in turn with a cool light and a warm sky; level 2 the same and a cone, a coloured object of any of the wheel's twelve hues; level 3 a ball under a coloured lamp of any hue on a coloured ground whose light bounces into its shadow.

How, first time: A form in coloured light; what a light's colour and the sky do to a local colour. The example plays on a form of the level, its edges and the pin printed: 1 the frame filled with the lit ground's colour; 2 the light side from the local colour toward the light; 3 the shadow side toward the sky's colour and darker; 4 the cast shadow from the ground toward the sky; (level 3) 5 the reflected light toward the ground's colour; Compare: the model's colours faint over the copy. One paragraph on mixing from the colours beside the frame; nothing of Compare.

The exercise: one frame; in it the form's visible edges printed grey, the pin (its top a dot) and its shadow, and faintly dashed where the families meet (the terminator and the cast shadow's outline: placing them is light on form's ability, this one is colour). Beside the frame at its top right the colours to mix from, each a swatch named under it: Local colour, Sunlight, Skylight (level 3: Lamplight and Ground). The tools: the wheel, Fill frame, Undo, Redo, Big, Small, Soft and the eyedropper; the eyedropper takes a swatch's colour whole.

Eyedropper on Sunlight, Fill frame: the frame the sun's colour, a stand-in for the lit ground. Eyedropper on Local colour, Small: the light side, the local colour unchanged (a mistake). Eyedropper on Skylight, Small: the shadow side and the cast shadow, the sky's colour only, not darker (a mistake).

Compare: the model's render laid over my copy at the slider, the form and the pin printed over it; the regions breaking a rule outlined red on the copy (here all three: the light side the local colour unchanged, the shadow side and the cast shadow the sky's colour, too light). The card: Colour under light 1; the hue and chroma disc with the given colours as squares and each of my regions as a dot in its colour, a thin dashed line from the local colour to the form's dots, the regions breaking a rule ringed red; Grey; One answer and Original shown; then Accurate, Almost, Again for me to choose. No reason line, no app result.
Slid to the end, the render shows whole. Grey: my copy and the render in grey, only the regions off in lightness outlined; Grey again: colour.
I choose Almost; it is kept. Finish: the lesson's end.
Level 2: a coloured object, its local colour beside the frame; level 3: a ball, Lamplight and Ground beside the frame, the How's fifth step the reflected light.
Reopen: Home leaves the lesson under way; Continue reopens it as it was.
